'''Theodore Garland Jr.''' (born 28 November 1956) is a [[biologist]] specializing in [[evolutionary physiology]] at the [[University of California, Riverside]].

== Education ==
Garland earned his B.S in [[zoology]] and M.S. in [[biology]] at the [[University of Nevada, Las Vegas]], working with William Glen Bradley, a [[mammalogist]], and his [[Ph.D.]] in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at the [[University of California, Irvine]] under [[Albert F. Bennett]], a comparative physiologist.

During his Master's degree, he served as President of the Southern Nevada Herpetology Association. During his Ph.D. work, he recorded the maximum speed (34.6&nbsp;km/h) of what to date remains the world's fastest lizard, ''[[Ctenosaura similis]]''. Subsequently, he completed postdoctoral training at the [[University of Washington]] with [[Raymond B. Huey]].

== Career ==
He was on the faculty at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] for 14 years, served as a program director for the Population Biology and Physiological Ecology Program<ref>{{Cite journal |jstor = 1308755|title = The First Three Years of NSF's Population Biology and Physiological Ecology Program|journal = BioScience|volume = 32|issue = 1|pages = 51–53|last1 = Kaufman|first1 = Donald W.|last2 = Courtney|first2 = Mark W.|last3 = Chu|first3 = Penn R.|year = 1982|doi = 10.2307/1308755}}</ref> at the [[National Science Foundation]] during 1991–1992, and is currently Distinguished Professor of Biology at the [[University of California, Riverside]] in the [https://eeob.ucr.edu/ Department of Evolution, Ecology, and Organismal Biology].

Garland is Editor in Chief of the journal ''[[Ecological and Evolutionary Physiology]]'', formerly ''[[Physiological and Biochemical Zoology]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.press.uchicago.edu/journals/pbz/board.html?journal=pbz |title=''Physiological and Biochemical Zoology'' Editorial Board |publisher=journals.uchicago.edu |access-date=2014-07-15}}</ref>
He is an Associate Editor for ''[[Behavior Genetics (journal)|Behavior Genetics]]'' and on the Editorial Advisory Board of [[Zoology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/zoology/editorial-board/|title=Editorial Board - Zoology - Journal - Elsevier}}</ref>  Garland is a former Topic Editor for ''[[Comprehensive Physiology]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wiley.com/WileyCDA/Section/id-404522.html |title=Comprehensive Physiology list of editors |publisher=Wiley.com |access-date=2013-09-24}}</ref> and has been on the editorial boards of the ''[[Journal of Morphology]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/35280/home?CRETRY=1&SRETRY=0 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20110414142648/http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/35280/home?CRETRY=1&SRETRY=0 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2011-04-14 |title=Journal of Morphology |publisher=.interscience.wiley.com |access-date=2013-09-24}}</ref> ''[[The American Naturalist]]'', and ''[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://biology.ucr.edu/people/faculty/Garland/GarlandCV.html|title = Garland Curriculum Vitae Ted Garland CV Theodore Garland CV Evolution Physiological Ecology Evolutionary Physiology Comparative Physiology Exercise Physiology Animal Behavior Quantitative Genetics Biostatistics Herpetology Locomotion Conservation Biology Phenotypic Plasticity Adaptive Plasticity}}</ref> He was an associate director for the ''Network for Experimental Research on Evolution'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nere.bio.uci.edu/ |title=NERE Home Page |publisher=Nere.bio.uci.edu |date=2004-01-01 |access-date=2013-09-24}}</ref> a University of California Multicampus Research Program.

His major scientific contributions have been in the areas of [[lizard]] locomotor [[physiology]] and [[ecology]], [[allometry]], [[phylogenetic comparative methods]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mesquiteproject.org/pdap_mesquite/index.html|title=Mesquite:PDAP:PDTree|author=Peter E. Midford|publisher=Mesquiteproject.org|access-date=2013-09-24}}</ref> and the application of [[artificial selection]] experiments to understand the correlated evolution of [[physiology]] and [[behavior]], as well as the physiological, neurobiological, and [[genetics|genetic]] bases of voluntary activity levels ([[physical exercise]]).

==Research==
Most generally, Garland is known for helping to found the field of evolutionary physiology, which attempts to combine the questions and approaches of [[Evolution | evolutionary biology]] with those of [[Comparative_physiology | comparative physiology]] and [[ecophysiology]], and for various studies of [[Complex_traits | complex traits]].  He has also studied [[Trade-off | trade-offs]] in various systems.

His research has generally fallen into three categories:  locomotor physiology of [[lizards]] and [[snakes]]; the development, testing, and application of [[phylogenetic comparative methods]]; and development of the selectively bred [[Experimental_evolution#High Runner laboratory house mice | High Runner mice]].

Recent studies have explored the [[genetic architecture]] of the [https://sites.google.com/ucr.edu/hrmice/home High Runner lines of mice], as well as the effects of early-life exposure to [[Diet_(nutrition) | diet]] and the opportunity for voluntary [[exercise]] on [[adult]] traits related to exercise behavior and physiology.  The latter studies fall under the general heading of [[phenotypic plasticity]] and [[epigenetics]].

==Awards==
In 1983–84, he was a Visiting [[Fulbright Scholar]] at the [[University of Wollongong]], [[Australia]], hosted by [https://web.archive.org/web/20130927092031/http://www.biomedexperts.com/Profile.bme/597501/Anthony_J_Hulbert Anthony J. Hulbert], and in 1985 he received the Outstanding Graduate Student Scholar Award from U.C., Irvine.

In 1991, he received a ''Presidential Young Investigator Award''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward.do?AwardNumber=9157268 |title=Presidential Young Investigator Award |publisher=Nsf.gov |access-date=2013-09-24}}</ref> from the [[National Science Foundation]].

In 2011, he was named a Hansen Distinguished Lecturer by the [[University of California, Berkeley]].

The [[University of Nevada, Las Vegas]] named him ''College of Sciences Alumnus of the Year''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.unlv.edu/news/article/success-competitive-career |title=College of Sciences Alumnus of the Year |date=25 April 2017 |publisher=unlv.edu |access-date=2018-06-25}}</ref> in April 2017.

In 2023, he received the Doctoral Dissertation Advisor/Mentoring Award from U.C., Riverside.

In 2025, he was named the [[August Krogh]] Distinguished Lecturer by the American Physiological Society.
